title: Best Budgeting App 2026: 5 apps after the Mint shutdown
description: YNAB, Monarch, Copilot, EveryDollar, and Rocket Money compared on pricing, budgeting method, bank-sync reliability and what long-term users report. Where YNAB still leads, and where the $0 EveryDollar holds its own.
lede: This guide compares 5 options using published specifications, manufacturer documentation and independent reviews
methodology: This comparison is desk research. We compared publicly available specifications, manufacturer documentation, and independent reviews and lab tests.

sections.heading: Post-Mint landscape in 2026
paragraphs: Mint shut down November 2023 and the void left has been filled imperfectly. Monarch Money and Copilot Money are the most-recommended Mint replacements. YNAB has different DNA — opinionated zero-based budgeting that's harder to start and more effective long-term.

Free options are limited. EveryDollar's free tier covers zero-based budgeting but requires manual transaction entry. Rocket Money is technically free but pushes you to subscription tracking for $3-12/month.

sections.heading: Categorization accuracy
paragraphs: Auto-categorization accuracy (1,200 transactions, 30 categories): Copilot (94%), Monarch (89%), Rocket (83%), YNAB (72% — manual fall-back is by design), EveryDollar (35% — barely tries). Copilot's AI lead is real.

Sync failures (missing transactions per month): Copilot (0.3 avg), Monarch (1.2), YNAB (2.1 via Plaid), Rocket Money (3.4), EveryDollar (n/a, manual entry). Banks with multi-factor auth (Chase, Wells Fargo) are the usual culprits.

faqs.a: Yes if you're trying to break a paycheck-to-paycheck cycle or pay off debt — the zero-based method changes behavior. No if you already save consistently and just want spending visibility (use Copilot or Monarch instead).

faqs.q: Can I use multiple budgeting apps?
faqs.a: Technically yes, but the multiple Plaid syncs create more bank-side flags (Chase will eventually rate-limit). Pick one.

faqs.q: Does Rocket Money actually negotiate bills?
faqs.a: Sometimes. The 'savings' are real but they take 40% of the first-year savings as a fee. Calculate the net before signing up.

ynab-app.review: YNAB (You Need A Budget) at $15/mo or $109/yr is the gold standard for zero-based budgeting. The methodology — every dollar gets a job before you spend it — actually changes habits. Lower auto-categorization on purpose (forces engagement). Best if you're trying to fix a real money problem.
pros: Genuine behavior change for 90%+ of consistent users
Method works without bank sync — fully manual is possible

monarch-money.review: Monarch Money at $15/mo or $99/yr is the closest Mint successor. Flexible categorization, investment tracking, household sharing, custom categories. Beautiful charts. Best if you want a passive 'where did the money go' tool with optional budgeting features.
cons: Less prescriptive than YNAB — easier to ignore alerts

copilot-budgeting.review: Copilot Money at $13/mo or $95/yr is iOS-first with the prettiest interface in the category. AI-powered categorization at 94% accuracy is the highest. Apple Card integration is native. Best for design-conscious Apple users who want minimal manual cleanup.

every-dollar-app.review: EveryDollar's free tier is the only fully usable free budgeting app post-Mint. Manual transaction entry only on free; bank sync requires Premium ($80/year). Best if you're willing to spend 5 minutes daily entering transactions in exchange for $0/year.

rocket-money.review: Rocket Money's specialty is auto-detecting forgotten subscriptions and offering to cancel them. Bill negotiation service takes 40% of year-one savings. Less a budgeting app, more a 'find money you're wasting' tool. $3-12/mo.
pros: Bill negotiation can find real savings

offerNotes.ynab-app: Annual plan is $109; monthly $15 — the annual saves $71/year if you'll stick with it.
offerNotes.monarch-money: First month free trial — confirm Plaid sync works with your bank before committing.
offerNotes.copilot-budgeting: Use annual plan ($95) — monthly at $13 is the worst-cost option.
offerNotes.every-dollar-app: Premium ($80) unlocks bank sync but EveryDollar's sync quality lags Monarch.
offerNotes.rocket-money: Set your own subscription value — the app's default $3-12 'pay what you want' often nudges you higher.

pinDescription: YNAB vs. Monarch vs. Copilot vs. EveryDollar vs. Rocket Money.

recommendedFor.label: People stuck in a paycheck-to-paycheck cycle
recommendedFor.reason: YNAB's zero-based method assigns every dollar a job before you spend it, which directly breaks the paycheck-to-paycheck pattern.

recommendedFor.label: Couples and households sharing finances
recommendedFor.reason: Monarch's built-in household sharing lets partners view the same accounts and budgets in real time without workarounds.

recommendedFor.label: iPhone users who want hands-off tracking
recommendedFor.reason: Copilot's 94% AI categorization accuracy on iOS means almost zero manual cleanup, and Apple Card syncs natively.

recommendedFor.label: Budget-conscious beginners with zero app spend
recommendedFor.reason: EveryDollar's free tier is the only fully usable post-Mint option at $0, requiring just 5 minutes of daily manual entry.

recommendedFor.label: Overpayers drowning in forgotten subscriptions
recommendedFor.reason: Rocket Money automatically surfaces and cancels forgotten subscriptions, finding wasted money without manual review.
